headline: Palworld Online launches on iOS & Android later this year as a new MMORPG
summary: Garena is developing Palworld Online, reimagining the original PC game's depth and freedom for mobile with a touch-friendly interface and new story elements.
details: Palworld is expanding to mobile with a new open-world MMORPG called Palworld Online, set to launch on iOS and Android later this year. Garena is developing the game, aiming to bring the original PC title's depth and freedom to mobile.

The mobile version will retain core features like crafting, creature collecting, and multiplayer options for co-op, PvP, and PvE. It will also introduce a new narrative setting with original story elements and side stories exclusive to this version.

Garena is designing a streamlined, touch-friendly interface with optional one-tap controls to optimize base management for various mobile screen sizes. A specific release date has not yet been announced, but it is expected this year.

headline_marked: [[Flock's CEO faced user]] after cameras led to wrongful stop and public backlash
headline: Flock's CEO faced user after cameras led to wrongful stop and public backlash
summary: Flock Safety's CEO, Garrett Langley, sat down with a user whose family was wrongly stopped by police due to their AI-powered cameras. They discussed privacy concerns, calls for regulation, and public backlash.
details: The CEO of Flock Safety, Garrett Langley, recently sat down for a candid discussion with a user whose family was wrongly stopped by police due to the company's AI-powered cameras. This incident, involving a $155,000 Range Rover, garnered millions of views and highlighted the exponential impact of Flock's technology.

The interview on The Drivecast podcast delved into the public backlash over privacy and Fourth Amendment concerns, growing calls for regulation, and Langley's controversial past comment labeling vandals of Flock equipment as 'domestic terrorists'.

Reports frequently detail instances of police misusing Flock's tech to stalk individuals, leading to arrests, misread situations, and heated city council meetings. This has also fueled a trend of people targeting and destroying the automatic license plate readers.

Despite leading a company at the forefront of automotive surveillance, Langley revealed he is not a 'car guy,' having driven the same Toyota Prius for years. He even retrofitted his own car with Apple CarPlay, showcasing a personal interest in tech integration.
